hook: Hear a literary episode once and follow it from facts to symbol to meaning: a packed suitcase that waited thirty-one years.
intro: A literary reading (Lesung), heard once: an author reads a complete episode from a novel about Anton and a brown leather suitcase that has stood on the bedroom wardrobe for thirty-one years, packed in one night in March 1993 and never unpacked. The text moves in three steps, and the questions follow them. First the concrete: numbers, dates, objects and actions (einunddreißig Jahre, März 1993, zwei Hemden, ein Wörterbuch, die Fotografie seiner Mutter, the tag WIEN – MONTREAL, two moves). Then the symbolic object: the suitcase becomes a weathervane (Wetterfahne) pointing west, and small details such as „Er war leichter, als er ihn in Erinnerung hatte“ prepare the meaning. Finally the text interprets itself, twice, with „nicht …, sondern …“ – and the answer is always the sondern-half, never the negated noun. The last paragraph shows the consequence in actions, not words. Listen for numbers first, then for the image, then for the antithesis, and keep listening to the last line.
tips[0].title: Concrete first: numbers, dates, objects
tips[0].text: The factual questions come from the first two paragraphs: how long, when, what was packed, what happened at the moves, how Ruth reacted. Note them before the images take over – a literary text rarely repeats its facts.
tips[0].check.why: neunzehn is 19 (neunzig is 90); catch numbers the first time, because a literary text rarely repeats them.
tips[1].title: The symbolic object: image + „solange …“
tips[1].text: The narrator turns the suitcase into something else with a „kein …, sondern …“ and then explains the image in the next clause. Paraphrase the image in abstract terms (a direction that stays open), not in literal ones (a plan to emigrate).
tips[1].check.why: The kein …, sondern … turns the lamp into an image, and the solange-clause explains it: as long as it burns, the waiting goes on.
tips[1].visual.moves[0].label: Fact
tips[1].visual.moves[1].label: Symbol
tips[1].visual.moves[2].label: Meaning
tips[2].title: The text interprets itself: nicht …, sondern …
tips[2].text: Near the end the text names its own meaning in an antithesis. The negated half is the tempting wrong answer (eine Reise, Kanada); the sondern-half is the interpretation the question asks for.
tips[2].trap: Kanada is the most memorable word in the text – and it stands in the negated half. Do not pick an answer just because it contains the word you remember.
tips[2].check.why: The meaning lies in the sondern-half; the negated noun (das Meer) is the tempting wrong answer.
tips[3].title: The ending speaks in actions
tips[3].text: The last paragraph contains no commentary, only actions. Ask what each action means: unpacking, putting things in their place, the empty suitcase in the cellar, the tag cut off.
tips[3].check.why: Crossing out the name and throwing the letter away unread are actions that end a connection; the text needs no comment.
remember[0]: Facts first (einunddreißig Jahre, März 1993, die Beförderung), then the image (die Wetterfahne), then the antithesis.
remember[1]: In „nicht …, sondern …“ the answer is the sondern-half; the negated noun (Kanada, eine Reise) is the trap.
remember[2]: Small physical details (leichter, als er ihn in Erinnerung hatte) prepare the interpretation.
remember[3]: A quiet ending in actions is still a statement: read what the actions mean.
exam: Literary texts read aloud appear in C2 exam listening — and at every Lesung in a bookshop, library or literature festival.
tips[1].check.q: „Das Licht im Fenster war keine Lampe mehr, sondern ein Versprechen: Solange es brannte, wartete jemand.“ What does the light stand for?
tips[1].check.options[2]: Someone promised to buy a lamp.
tips[2].check.q: „Nicht das Meer hatte sie zurückgehalten, sondern die Angst, alles zu verlieren.“ What held her back?
tips[3].check.q: Last lines of a story: „Er strich ihren Namen aus seinem Adressbuch und warf den Brief ungeöffnet weg.“ What do the actions say?
tips[3].check.options[0]: He has broken off contact with her.
tips[3].check.answer: He has broken off contact with her.
